chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Sa'id ibn Khuthaym, from Ma'mar ibn Khuthaym, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is your kunya (nomine)?' I said, 'I have not yet taken a kunya, for I have no son, no wife, and no female slave.' He said, 'What prevents you from doing so?' I said, 'A hadith reached me from Ali (peace be upon him).' He said, 'And what is it?' I said, 'It reached us from Ali (peace be upon him) that he said: He who takes a kunya but has no family/children is Abu Ja'ar (a derogatory term implying barrenness or lack of lineage).' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'It is a slight (shawn); this is not from the hadith of Ali (peace be upon him). Indeed, we give our children their kunya while they are young, fearing the stigma of 'al-nabaz' ( being labeled as 'the one without offspring') so that it does not attach to them.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْرٍ: A derogatory term for a man without children, implying barrenness
key_terms.أَهْلٌ: Family, specifically referring to children/offspring in this context
key_terms.النَّبَزِ: Stigma or labeling, specifically 'nabaz bi-la walad' (being labeled as childless)
key_terms.تُكَنَّى: To take or be given a kunya (nomine)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Abu Ja'ar' and why did the Imams give kunya to children while they were young?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) corrects the attribution of the derogatory term 'Abu Ja'ar' (the one without children) to Imam Ali, clarifying that it refers to actual childlessness rather than a lack of offspring at the time of naming. He explains that the Prophet and Imams often bestowed kunyas on children in their youth to preemptively shield them from the social stigma of being labeled 'childless' if they remained unmarried or had no children later in life. This highlights the Shia scholarly view of kunya as a dynamic social identifier rather than a fixed biological status.
